trends.name: Iran Strait of Hormuz Crisis Escalation
trends.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards declared the Strait of Hormuz closed with threats of 'harsh measures' against shipping, escalating military tensions beyond Trump's diplomatic efforts. Multiple U.S. officials confirm no viable military solution exists to quickly reopen the waterway, creating sustained geopolitical supply-chain risk. Oil markets responding with prices climbing toward $110+ and potential $200 risk flagged.

trends.name: US Military Buildup Middle East Expansion
trends.summary: Trump administration considering deployment of up to 10,000 additional ground troops to Middle East on top of existing 5,000 Marines and 82nd Airborne, signaling sustained military commitment amid Iran tensions. This represents major escalation in military posture with broad implications for defense budgets and geopolitical risk premiums.

trends.name: Mega-Cap Tech Concentration Risk (NVDA/MSFT)
trends.summary: Nvidia and Microsoft now represent 14-15% of S&P 500 composition, with ~$30 trillion in U.S. retirement accounts (401k, SEP, IRA) holding S&P 500 as core holdings. This creates colossal wealth concentration risk where market movements in two stocks cascade through majority of retirement savings.

trends.name: Oil Price Surge Driven by Geopolitical Risk
trends.summary: Brent crude topping $110 amid Iran crisis, with firms flagging potential $200 risk if Strait of Hormuz fully closes. Treasury Secretary downplaying 'choke point' narrative contradicts market pricing, suggesting inflation fears despite arguments that higher oil may not trigger broad CPI spikes.

trends.name: Nasdaq 100 Stagnation After 100-Day Underperformance
trends.summary: Nasdaq 100 has traded below all-time highs for 100 consecutive days, longest streak since 2023, while remaining only -10% off peak—a rare pattern (6th time since 1985) historically associated with subsequent volatility. Market concentration in mega-cap tech combined with stagnation signals potential rotation opportunity or further downside.

trends.name: European Bond Market Stress & Rate Hike Expectations
trends.summary: European borrowing costs hit 15-year highs as investors brace for ECB rate hikes. ECB's Müller signals impatience waiting for 'second round effects' to fully materialize, suggesting faster tightening cycle ahead. This divergence from U.S. policy creates currency and capital flow implications.

trends.name: Pension Fund Equity Rotation & Q1 Rebalancing
trends.summary: Goldman Sachs estimates U.S. pension funds will purchase +$13.8 billion of equities by quarter-end, largest monthly purchase in 97% of historical comparisons (since 2000). Simultaneously, gold saw largest outflow since October 2025 ($6.3bn from GLD), signaling major institutional reallocation from safe havens to equities.

trends.name: Private Credit Market Stress & Bank Comeback
trends.summary: Cracks emerging in private credit sector (e.g., Blue Owl's $1.4B asset sale disappointing markets) are opening door for traditional Wall Street banks to recapture lending business. Confidence in private credit 'empire' weakening as unreported deal structures raise transparency concerns.

trends.name: AI Infrastructure & Power Supply Constraints
trends.summary: IREN positioned as winner in AI's most constrained resource (power), while Japan demand is now topping capacity since 2022 per revised BOJ data. CleanSpark seen as positioned for re-rating as AI demand builds, highlighting data center power infrastructure as critical bottleneck for AI expansion.

trends.name: Retail Real Estate Decline & K-Shaped Economy
trends.summary: Retail CRE (commercial real estate) transactions for shops and malls are plunging amid K-shaped economic bifurcation, where wealthy consumers and luxury retail diverge from mass-market retail. This reflects structural shift in consumer spending patterns and real estate valuations.

trends.name: SoftBank $40B OpenAI Bridge Facility & AI Investment War
trends.summary: SoftBank entering $40 billion bridge facility to fund OpenAI investment, escalating capital race in generative AI. This mega-commitment signals competitive intensity for AI leadership and potential valuation implications for AI startups and infrastructure providers.

trends.name: Bond Yields Rise vs Money Market Funds Opportunity
trends.summary: AGG (bond ETF) now yields >1 percentage point more than best money market funds (4.67% vs 3.58%), creating yield arbitrage opportunity as bond market offers better risk-adjusted returns. Reflects normalization of yield curve and potential rotation from cash equivalents into fixed income.
